correctness.rationale: The three forms are a regular sequence because the hyperplane quadratic form is nondegenerate and the quartic is nonzero at (1,-1,i,-i,0,...). Rank failure for the Jacobian (1,x,x^3) forces at most three coordinate values. The two-value case contradicts the first and second power sums. The depressed-cubic root relation combined with a strictly positive multiplicity-weighted square obstruction forces equal three multiplicities and the cubic-root orbit. Orbit size is n!/[3(a!)^3] after quotient by scalar cube-root rotations. At each point the constrained Hessian on W={sum v_i=sum x_i v_i=0} has radical exactly Cx, hence its projective restriction is nondegenerate. The resulting singularities are A1 nodes; the checker verified characteristic-prime sample ranks and small orbit counts, with the infinite proof independent of tests.

value.rationale: The exact singularity basket of a natural nonconsecutive power-sum complete intersection in every dimension is a motivated geometric invariant: it determines the smooth/nodal transition by n mod 3, the full orbit enumeration, and total Milnor number, whereas general ideal-theoretic literature establishes only regularity and normality. The low-dimensional 30-node antecedent supports naturality, and the n>=9 infinite family is new information under the documented comparison, with no dependence on an unmotivated chosen finite slice.
